//: The MARKETING project (imagehorse.app). Its Vercel Root Directory is
marketing/, so this file — not the repo root one — configures it. The root
vercel.json is the EDITOR (edit.imagehorse.app) and roots at the repo root,
because the Rust crate, rust-toolchain.toml and scripts/ all live there.
THERE IS NO CATCH-ALL REWRITE, deliberately. scripts/prerender.mjs emits a
real file per route, so a /(.*) -> /index.html fallback would answer junk
URLs with the home page at 200 — a soft 404. Unmatched paths fall through
to dist/404.html with a real 404 instead.

redirects.//: One hostname holds the ranking signal. www is a separate origin to a crawler, so it is redirected rather than served — permanently (308), so the redirect itself is what gets cached and indexed. The apex is canonical because that is what src/seo.ts writes into every <link rel=canonical> and every sitemap entry; changing one without the other splits the site in two.

headers.//: `.app` is on the HSTS preload list at the TLD, so browsers already refuse plaintext here — this header is what keeps that true if the site ever moves to a domain that isn't.

headers.value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com; font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com data:; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'

headers.//: The SAFE default, deliberately applied to everything and then narrowed below. It is the right value for the HTML: those filenames are stable across deploys, so a cached copy would keep pointing at the previous build's hashed assets. Matching on a .html suffix instead does NOT work here — a prerendered route is requested as /features, with no extension, and only resolves to features/index.html after this stage.

ORDER MATTERS: this rule also matches /(.*) above, and Vercel applies every matching rule in order with the last write of a given header winning. So this must stay BELOW the block that sets the default, or the assets get max-age=0. Everything under /assets/ carries a content hash in its filename, so a changed file is a changed URL and this can never serve a stale one; `immutable` additionally stops the revalidation request browsers make on reload, which is a real repeat-visit difference.
Same ordering rule. An hour is long enough to absorb a crawl spike and short enough that a new page shows up in the next fetch.

The share cards and icons change only when scripts/gen-og-images.mjs is re-run, and a scraper refetching one on every unfurl is pure waste. A day, not a year: unlike /assets/ these filenames are NOT content-hashed, so a stale copy is possible and should expire on its own.
